To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the gelation kinetics of polysaccharide gels induced by divalent cation was investigated by viscoelastic measurements; (2) the gel front migration during the gelation was studied for the first time by turbidity measurements; (3) the gelation mechanism was proposed.

The gelation kinetics of polyGal hydrogels induced by various divalent cation was investigated by both visco-elastic and turbidity techniques and it was demonstrated for the first-time the gel front migration by the spatiotempo-ral variation of turbidity.

the gel front migration is characterized by the presence or not of a peak at sol/gel interface which is correlated to the gel formation and the gelation mechanism is based on the presence or not a threshold molar ration R*.

the gelation process of polyGal hydrogels induced by various divalent cationic species was strongly dependent on the nature of cation.

the gel front migration in the cation-induced polysaccaride hydrogels is governed by a competition between two opposite phenomena: the gel front contraction induced by the formation of crosslinks and the gel front expansion induced by the diffusion of cations.
the gel front migration in polyGal hydrogels is a function of the nature of the divalent cations and the initial cation concentrations.

the gelation kinetics and the gel front migration were affected by the nature of cation.
the gel front migration is a function of the nature of cation and the molar ratio R*.
